title: Running Config vs Startup Config
description: Understand the difference between running-config and startup-config and how to manage both.
scenario: Understand the difference between running-config and startup-config and how to manage both.

steps.title: Inspect the switch
steps.instruction: The switch boots from what is saved in NVRAM, so right now RAM and NVRAM hold exactly the same thing. Run both show commands and watch the terminal.
steps.outcome: ✓ Both copies inspected — they are identical.

steps.title: Make a change
steps.instruction: Add VLAN 20 on FastEthernet0/3. Changes hit the running-config (RAM) immediately — compare the green and amber cards below to see the startup-config stay behind.
steps.hint: Step 2 wants: the Add VLAN button
steps.outcome: ✓ Configuration changed successfully. running-config updated — startup-config unchanged.

steps.title: Compare and save
steps.instruction: The green card (RAM) has VLAN 20, the amber card (NVRAM) does not. Save with write memory so the change survives a reboot — then both copies match again.
steps.outcome: ✓ Saved to NVRAM — both copies match, your change survives a reboot.

concepts.title: Running Config
concepts.body: The running-config is the active configuration stored in RAM. Changes take effect immediately.
concepts.code:
SW1# show running-config
! Active configuration — lives in RAM

concepts.title: Startup Config
concepts.body: The startup-config is stored in NVRAM. It loads into RAM when the switch boots.
concepts.code:
SW1# show startup-config
! Boot configuration — lives in NVRAM

concepts.title: Saving & Restoring
concepts.body: Use "write memory" or "copy running-config startup-config" to save. Use "copy startup-config running-config" to restore.
concepts.code:
Save:   write memory
Restore: copy startup-config running-config
